anti_overlap: Does not evaluate the shadewright-lint.ts check implementations themselves (vacuous or evadable regex checks) — that is fd-staticanalysis-tokenlint-evasion.
Does not evaluate the seven-interaction-state derivation, component contracts, or the /plan page's non-map wiring — that is fd-uistatemachine-contract-fidelity.

Scoped to the getComputedStyle/CSS-cascade↔MapLibre/SVG runtime seam specifically: token resolution timing, theme-change propagation, and cross-consumer synchronization — not general MapLibre API usage or map UX.
decision_lens: For every value shadewright-map.ts resolves via token()/getComputedStyle, trace every place it is consumed and ask: what event actually re-triggers this read; does that event fire before or after the CSS backing it is attached/updated; and is there a sibling element in the same render that resolves the 'same' value through a live CSS var() instead — if so, do the two ever visibly disagree after a theme change?
focus: shadewright-map.ts's getComputedStyle(document.documentElement) seam — the single point where CSS custom properties are frozen into JS values for MapLibre and the SVG fallback — and every place that seam can silently diverge from the live cascade: theme-change staleness, SSR/hydration timing, the never-triggered data-sw-theme attribute, and the split between CSS-var-resolved and JS-resolved siblings inside the same component.
name: fd-cssvar-mapseam-runtime-integrity
persona: Apply the perspective of a rendering-pipeline engineer who has shipped theme-aware WebGL/canvas overlays on top of a CSS-driven design system (map SDKs, canvas dashboards, native-bridge UIs) and has been burned specifically by the class of bug where 'read the computed style once, cache it in a paint object' quietly stops tracking the DOM the moment a CSS custom property changes underneath it. This reviewer's default assumption about any getComputedStyle call is that it is already stale by the time it is read, and audits every consumer for whether it re-resolves on the right triggers, in the right order, relative to style attachment, hydration, and theme flips.
review_areas: components/RouteMap.tsx's `RouteSketch` renders its polyline `stroke` via `routeLineColor(band)` — a JS-resolved, render-time-frozen hex from getComputedStyle — while its start/end marker `<circle>` fills use literal `var(--color-shade)` / `var(--color-extreme)` CSS references resolved live by the browser, in the same `<svg>`. RouteMap has no state or effect that re-renders RouteSketch on a theme change with stable path/band props, and its `onThemeChange` subscription lives only inside the live-MapLibre branch's effect (never wired to the `liveFailed` SVG-fallback path) — so the line and its own endpoints can visibly disagree on theme after a flip.

`isDark()` / `onThemeChange()` (shadewright-map.ts ~38-44, 191-223) branch on `document.documentElement.getAttribute("data-sw-theme")`, and the CSS's `:root[data-sw-theme="dark"]` override block, the dark-trigger-parity lint test, and the MutationObserver's `attributeFilter: ["data-sw-theme"]` all exist specifically so a manual override can win over the OS preference (R13.3) — but grep the app: nothing anywhere ever calls `setAttribute("data-sw-theme", ...)`. The entire manual-override code path (in this file, in the CSS, and in the lint test that checks the two dark blocks 'agree') proves two static artifacts are consistent with each other while proving nothing about whether a real user can ever reach the state either encodes.

`token()` returns `""` for every property when `typeof window === "undefined"`, and several call sites fold that into a fallback via `||` (`routeLineColor`'s `token(...) || token("--sw-color-route-neutral")`, `routeLinePaint`'s `Number(token(...)) || 5`) — the same falsy-coalescing fires identically whether the CSS variable is genuinely absent/zero OR simply not yet attached to the document (stylesheet still loading, code-split CSS racing the dynamic `import("maplibre-gl/dist/maplibre-gl.css")`). Trace whether PlanMap's mount effect, which calls `mapStyleUrl()` synchronously before any paint, can ever run ahead of shadewright.tokens.css's `:root` block being attached in a slow-network or code-split load order.

`keepLayerMounted`'s `draw()` closure re-derives `routeLinePaint(band)` — a fresh getComputedStyle read — on every one of four listened events (`load`, `styledata`, `sourcedata`, `idle`) for the life of the map. Confirm this doesn't reintroduce forced synchronous style recalculation (layout thrash) during a busy map session with frequent `sourcedata` firing (tile loads), which the canon's own tempo/motion concerns (§10) would flag as a performance regression distinct from correctness.

PlanMap.tsx's `drawRoute` unconditionally re-applies paint via `setPaintProperty` on every call regardless of whether the layer already existed, while RouteMap.tsx's `ensureRoute` only calls `routeLinePaint(band)` inside the `!m.getLayer?.("route-line")` guard (i.e. only on first creation, relying on `setStyle`-triggered layer teardown/recreate to pick up a new theme). Confirm these two consumers of the same seam don't have divergent repaint guarantees under rapid or overlapping theme-flip + style-load events (e.g. the OS theme flipping twice within one map style-load cycle).

shadewright-map.ts's own docstring (lines 10-18) claims the impure getComputedStyle half is cleanly split from the pure, testable half (dashToSvg/parseDashToken/drawnFraction, covered in shadewright-map.test.ts) — but `RouteSketch`'s `sketchDash = band ? dashToSvg(routeDashArray(band), SKETCH_STROKE) : undefined` calls `routeDashArray`, which calls `token()`, inline during JSX render, not confined to an effect. The 'impure read' is not actually isolated from React's render scheduling in this consumer, so its staleness properties are governed by whatever causes RouteSketch to re-render — which, per the first review area, is nothing, on a theme-only change.

severity_examples.condition: components/RouteMap.tsx's `RouteSketch` (~lines 241-260) draws the route via `stroke: routeLineColor(band)` (frozen at last render) while its two marker circles use live `var(--color-shade)`/`var(--color-extreme)`. If the OS theme flips while a fallback sketch is already showing (MapLibre failed to load) and path/band stay unchanged, nothing re-renders RouteSketch: the markers repaint to dark mode instantly via the CSS cascade while the connecting line keeps the light-theme hex indefinitely — a themed line whose own endpoints read as the wrong theme relative to it, directly contradicting the file's stated goal ('the map inherits both themes like everything else,' line 13) in precisely the renderer that has no MapLibre styledata event to lean on for a fix.
severity_examples.scenario: RouteSketch's own route line and endpoint markers can disagree on theme

severity_examples.condition: `data-sw-theme` is read by isDark()/onThemeChange(), encoded in the CSS `:root[data-sw-theme="dark"]` block, and asserted for cross-block parity by the sw-contrast lint test — but no file in apps/solwend-web ever calls `setAttribute("data-sw-theme", ...)`. R13.3's 'explicit override wins in both directions' is canon-promised, CSS-encoded, and lint-verified for internal consistency, yet a user cannot actually force dark or light mode independent of the OS today; nothing flags this as a missing feature rather than a passing test suite.
severity_examples.scenario: The manual dark-mode override is fully wired in code and CSS but has no reachable trigger

severity_examples.condition: Every `||` fallback in shadewright-map.ts (lines ~24-29, 67-69, 109-113, 129) treats an SSR-time empty read identically to a genuinely-zero or unset custom property, so a slow-loading stylesheet on a cold cache would silently render a default color/width rather than surfacing 'tokens not ready yet' — worth confirming whether Next.js's static-export CSS injection order can ever let PlanMap's mount effect observe an un-attached stylesheet.
severity_examples.scenario: token()'s empty-string fallback conflates 'not loaded yet' with 'legitimately absent'

success_hints: Force a theme change (toggle OS appearance, or fire the matchMedia listener manually) while a RouteMap fallback sketch is on screen with a stable path/band, and check whether the drawn line and its own endpoint markers agree on theme after the flip.

Grep the whole apps/solwend-web tree (and its consumers) for any setAttribute or state wiring that would ever set data-sw-theme on document.documentElement; if none exists, report the manual-override code path as unreachable — a state promised by canon/CSS/lint but not implemented in product.

Throttle the network (or inspect Next.js's CSS injection order) to see whether getComputedStyle calls in PlanMap's mount effect can ever observe an un-attached or default-UA stylesheet, and report what each token() call site returns and renders in that case.

Compare PlanMap.drawRoute's unconditional setPaintProperty-on-every-call strategy against RouteMap.ensureRoute's create-once-inside-getLayer-guard strategy for correctness under rapid or overlapping theme-flip and style-load events.

Treat every || fallback in shadewright-map.ts as a place where 'not ready yet' and 'legitimately absent' are being conflated, and look for a concrete input that makes the distinction visible to a real user.
task_context: find defects, gaps and false confidence in the Shadewright IMPLEMENTATION (not the canon, already reviewed). Focus: checks that pass vacuously or are trivially evaded; canon rules that NO check enforces; states declared but unreachable; the getComputedStyle token-resolution seam and its failure modes; and anywhere the enforcement suite reports green while the rendered page is wrong — three classes already silently compiled to nothing this session (a bad Tailwind border utility, an undefined `wide:` variant, and an undeclared --color-bg). Weight lib/shadewright-map.ts, components/PlanMap.tsx, and components/RouteMap.tsx most heavily; treat shadewright.tokens.css and shadewright-map.test.ts as the supporting artifacts that define what 'correct' already means for the pure half of this seam.
